overview.headline: Malaysian coral reefs face record heat stress in 2026, requiring urgent local management to mitigate cumulative damage.
key_findings: Sabah reefs are experiencing record heat stress in 2026, exceeding 2024 peaks with 13.4 DHW.
Average coral cover fell to 40% in 2025, the lowest level recorded between 2015 and 2025.
Local pressures, including anchor damage, are associated with 6 points less coral cover at affected islands.
Reefs show a clear association between higher previous-year heat stress and subsequent coral cover decline.
Trash reported at previous surveys is associated with a 3-point decline in coral cover.

Higher mean cover (44.9%) but vulnerable to local pressures during calm years.

overview.heat_outlook_2026: Sabah has reached record heat stress (13.4 DHW), while the Malacca Strait faces 9.0 DHW; these levels are associated with significant coral decline.
overview.caveats: Forecasts have a typical error of 6 points; small changes often reflect reefs drifting toward regional averages rather than specific local trends. Associations are based on observational data, not proven causes.
